chunks: Or to feed in times of famine

key_terms.مَسْغَبَةٍ: Famine / Scarcity of food / High prices

ai.seo_question: What does 'feeding in times of famine' refer to in Quranic Zakat rulings?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase from Surah Al-Balad is often linked to the specific context of the famine in Mecca, emphasizing that feeding the poor during 'masghabah' (a day of hunger or scarcity) is a direct path to spiritual elevation and divine proximity. Scholars highlight that this act of charity not only alleviates immediate physical suffering but also serves as a practical manifestation of the 'freeing of slaves' mentioned in Surah At-Takwir, representing the liberation of the soul from the bondage of material need.
